Quality Heartbeat

Fourteen independent tools in one file, from the Executive Summary through to the monthly reports. Everything runs in your browser — no workbook you upload and no table you load ever leaves this page.

1

Executive Summary

The front door, and the only tool that reads the shared tables directly rather than asking for an upload. Four sections — Audits & QC score (call and non-call side by side), Disputes, CRFs and Analyst productivity — each with its own filters, sortable columns and a “more detail” button through to the full report behind it. The KPI strip mirrors the WBR’s Enhanced Insights card for card, so the same number never reads two ways in two places.

2

Workforce Management

Reads the NPT and Leaves SharePoint exports and turns them into a management view of productive-time loss — NPT % per analyst, where the time goes by category, leave patterns, and true productive availability (scheduled − leave − NPT) on a daily, weekly, or monthly grain. Formerly Resource Allocation; its Overview page now lives on the Control page.

3

Assignment Distributor

Routes every active agent to a team and distributes audits by workload against real analyst capacity, honouring coaching conflicts and editable department/division eligibility rules. Handling time is measured per department and division, so a Creditor Correspondence call and a Settlement Processing review are never costed the same. Weekly distribute generates a fresh book; Daily rebalance takes yesterday's export and equalises remaining work across each team, inheriting the roster, exceptions, prior moves and holidays from that file — and handing an analyst their own agents back the day they return from leave.

4

QC Audits Merger

Merges audit exports across 23 SharePoint list types with source auto-detection and date & week filtering into one clean sheet. Excel (.xlsx, .xlsm, .xls) as well as CSV, and the merged result is previewed in the page before you download it.

5

Coaching List Builder

Builds the monthly coaching list from the Master Sheet and last month’s list, then schedules the sessions. Stage 1 rebuilds the month’s stats from the call date, applies each team’s eligibility bar, routes every agent to the team that owns their department, and assigns coaches under continuity, reservation and exclusion rules — exporting the workbook in the locked format with live formulas, plus the verification email for Operations. Stage 2 takes that same workbook back with Ops’ replies, reads their shift times however they sent them, and places three weekly sessions in Amman time inside every constraint, returning the file with every sheet intact. This tool carries its own two-stage sidebar, so it has no sub-tabs here.

6

Payments Auto Distribution

fxPick5 sampling. Four views — Agent List (the final output), Notes, Tasks, and the Distribution query builder. The Assigned analyst column on the Agent List is emitted as “-”: agents are assigned to analysts in general now, so the tool no longer rotates a name into it.

7

Seniors Tasks Tracker

The recurring-task calendar for the Quality Seniors, covering every assignment from May to December 2026. Each row carries its task, owner, due date, cadence (weekly, bi-daily, twice-a-week, monthly, or a named business day) and any reference sheet or video. Three views: Table for sorting and searching the full list, Cards for a scannable feed, and By senior for side-by-side columns showing who owns what. Filter by senior, task type or month, and today’s row is highlighted automatically. Built by Hamza Mehyar; the data is embedded, so nothing needs uploading.

8

Weekly Business Report

Upload the Master Sheet once and build both Call and Non-Call reports for the previous completed week. A Classic WBR section reproduces the standard tables, plus an Enhanced Insights layer of trend, risk, momentum, Pareto and coverage charts.

9

Audits Coaching Delivery

Reads the same Master Sheet as the WBR, but follows the Team Lead Action on every scorecard — what the lead actually did once Quality raised it. Calls and non-calls are merged natively. Classic reproduces the standard action tables and the flagged-vs-pending view; Enhanced Insights adds team-lead accountability, backlog ageing, a named chase list of what is actually stuck, auto-fail follow-through and dispute concentration. Only the five standard Team Lead Actions get a section of their own; anything else typed into that column is counted as unaddressed and reported once, as a remainder, so a stray name in SharePoint cannot fill the summary with bullets.

10

CRF Report

Reads the Coaching Request Form SharePoint export (.csv or .xlsx). A CRF is peer-reported quality — one team flagging that another team's agent left work in a state that caused them a problem. Classic covers raised, closed, pending by team lead, closing categories and repeat-agent outliers; Enhanced Insights adds the validation mix, reporting quality by raising lead, gap type by department, open-queue ageing and a chase list.

11

Dispute Validation Report

Reads the [Internal] Audit Dispute Form (ADF) export against the Master Sheet, which supplies the audit counts every percentage divides by. A dispute is a Team Lead contesting an audit score, and the process was designed with the lead as a filtration step — so the figure that matters is how many of those disputes the Quality senior then ruled invalid. Monthly, counted by audit date so a dispute always sits in the month of the audit it contests. Classic merges volume and outcome into one department table, adds the three-month view and the Team Lead and agent outlier lists; Enhanced Insights adds point of failure, grey-area share and per-senior consistency. Drop the quarterly Quality Audit Database alongside the Master Sheet to fill the older months.

12

Quality Monthly Report

The month per department from the Master Sheet — average score, evaluations and auto-fails — plus the split by audit type, in the two tables the monthly mail has always carried. Deliberately thin: no insights layer, because its value is that it does not change. Produces the email draft and the formatted workbook that goes attached to it.

13

Quality–L&D Alignment Report

Prepares the bi-weekly alignment with L&D. Takes the raw Audit & Coaching Center list exports — all of them at once, no consolidating — finds every scored (N Points) column on its own, and works out where each department lost the most of the points available to it. Ranking is on Loss % rather than raw points, because the same requirement is weighted differently on every scorecard. Incubation, Calibration, Test and L&D audits are excluded throughout. Sections: department gaps, per-family comparison with shared metrics first, the auditor comments behind each gap, and a fixed prompt plus a comment workbook for the theme write-up. Optionally compares against the previous period's snapshot.

14

Queue Health & Task Governance

Built by Osama Shahrour and folded into the hub in its own right. Three sub-tabs: Queue Health, Task Governance and Merge. It keeps its own workflow but wears the hub’s chrome, so the sidebar and theme are the same ones every other tool uses.

Sign-in, access and the Control page

A

Who can see what

Three access levels. Administrator gets every tool, the user list and the team structure. Quality team gets every tool and the shared files on Control, and can read the team structure but not change it. Executive gets the Executive Summary and the four reports it links out to. Access is checked when a tool opens, not just when the sidebar is drawn, so a link to a tool you are not entitled to does not open it.

B

The team structure

Analysts by senior, and the coaching teams with the departments each one audits. It lives on the Control page and is the single definition every tool reads — Workforce Management and the Coaching List Builder pick up a change the moment it is made. An administrator can add or remove a senior or a coaching team, rename either, drag analysts between columns, or add several at once. An analyst has exactly one senior, so moving them takes them off the previous column automatically.

C

Publishing a change

Edits to users and to the team structure are saved in your browser straight away, and nowhere else. Download updated file — on either section, they produce the same file — writes both back into a fresh copy of this page for you to republish to GitHub. Everyone picks the change up next time they open it. A published roster carries a revision number and overrules an older copy sitting in someone’s browser, which is what makes one publish enough.

Each tool is embedded in its own isolated frame, so their upload flows and internal state never collide. Sign-in is a lock, not a vault: there is no server behind it, so treat it as keeping the page tidy rather than as protecting anything confidential.
